title: Vishnupad Temple, Gaya - A Sacred Footprint of Lord Vishnu
content:
Vishnupad Temple, Gaya

The Vishnupad Temple in Gaya, Bihar, is one of the most revered Hindu temples in India. Situated on the banks of the Phalgu River, it is believed to enshrine the footprint of Lord Vishnu in solid rock. This temple holds immense significance for devotees performing Pind Daan, a ritual for the peace of ancestors’ souls.

History and Significance

According to Hindu mythology, the demon Gayasura was subdued by Lord Vishnu, who pressed his foot on the demon’s chest, leaving behind a divine footprint. The sacred spot became the foundation of the Vishnupad Temple.
The present structure was rebuilt in the 18th century by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore, who also restored several ancient temples across India. The name Vishnupad literally translates to “the footprint of Lord Vishnu.”

Architecture

Made entirely of gray granite stone, the temple features exquisite carvings and a 50-meter-high shikhara (spire) that dominates the skyline of Gaya. Inside the sanctum, the footprint of Lord Vishnu is covered with silver plating and surrounded by flowers and lamps. The temple complex also has smaller shrines dedicated to other deities, creating an atmosphere of deep spirituality.

Religious Importance

The Pind Daan ritual, performed to help ancestors attain moksha (salvation), is the main religious activity associated with Vishnupad Temple. Thousands of devotees from across India visit the temple, especially during the Pitru Paksha Mela, to perform these sacred rites along the banks of the Phalgu River.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March
